transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Ellen (CSM), Samir (Peregrine Head of ML), Jenna (Platform), Priya (Security), Liam (Product), Theo (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on rollout mechanics: canary thresholds, A/B fallback gating, telemetry expectations, zero-downtime traffic shift approach. Agreed action items and dry-run date.

Topics covered:
- Cutover choreography (staging -> prod)
- Canary metrics and success thresholds (latency, error rate, quality regressions)
- A/B fallback strategy and circuit breakers
- Security boundary checks (SOC2 scope, SSO, KMS)
- Runbook and dry-run timing

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everybody, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick round and then jump into the cutover plan.
[00:18] Samir Patel: thanks, Maya. we had a few flaps in staging last week so i'm keen to nail the rollback story.
[00:28] Carlos Rivera: yeah quick update from our side — we've tuned the batcher and lowered tail latency on the 4k sequences by about 12% in the last run, that should help the canary.
[00:42] Jenna Ortiz: great. question, are we still relying on the prefix K V cache? in the last run we saw some cache misses that spiked token cost.
[00:55] Carlos Rivera: good call, the KV cache — sometimes transcribed as K-V cache — we saw misses because prefixes weren't normalized. we've added a normalizer in the middleware so odds of those misses drop.
[01:12] Priya Nair: from security, quick: we need an explicit note of what remains in Redwood's hosted control plane vs what stays in our VPC for SOC2 scoping.
[01:28] Maya Chen: yes Priya, we'll add a diagram to the runbook and attach the SOC2 boundary doc. we'll also include the SSO test steps for the dry-run.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: product question — for A/B, can we do percent-based routing at edge and fall back to older model if quality drops? how fast is the rollback?
[01:54] Carlos Rivera: you can route by percent; Redwood supports traffic steering by model variant. rollback is immediate — we can flip the routing policy, but we also recommend a circuit-breaker on elevated error rate to auto-fallback.
[02:10] Theo Marsh: how are you measuring quality regressions? we need deterministic checks, not just human review.
[02:20] Carlos Rivera: agreed. our suggestion is a small held-out eval set (the 50 smoke tests Jenna mentioned), plus token-level diffs and semantic drift metrics logged to the console.
[02:34] Samir Patel: can we capture hallucination rate with heuristics? we've had false positives but it's ok as a signal.
[02:42] Maya Chen: yes, heuristics plus a manual spot-check cadence during the canary window. we'll show sample dashboards in the dry-run.
[02:55] Jenna Ortiz: timeline check — we want zero-downtime if possible; meaning no user-facing errors. how do you do a zero-downtime shift with long-lived KV caches?
[03:08] Carlos Rivera: two options — warm-cache prefill in staging, or progressive ramp where we route a small percent to new model and warm caches as requests flow. both require sticky routing handling for sessions.
[03:23] Jenna Ortiz: ok sticky routing is doable but needs session affinity at edge.
[03:29] Speaker 7: (inaudible) ...affinity config is on our side.
[03:36] Maya Chen: good. on monitoring, we propose SLOs: 95p latency < 450ms, error rate < 0.8% for the canary, and semantic regression < 3% on eval set. those are starting points — open to adjustments.
[03:56] Samir Patel: latency numbers looks reasonable. cost is a factor too — any guidance on cost delta during canary?
[04:04] Carlos Rivera: expect a temporary +10-25% token cost during ramp depending on cache warm-up and traffic duplication for A/B. Optimize by enabling prefix caching and lower precision quantization for the canary variant if acceptable.
[04:20] Priya Nair: KMS question: are keys kept in our HSM? we need to confirm integration.
[04:27] Maya Chen: yes we support customer-managed keys; we'll include the KMS integration doc link in the follow-up.
[04:34] Liam O'Connor: curious on autoscaling — what's the expected spin-up time for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:41] Carlos Rivera: Dedicated pools can scale predictably given reserved slots, but spin-up for new instance types does take minutes. Hosted has faster warm pools but less predictable for large spikes. For cutover we recommend pre-provisioned safety capacity.
[05:00] Jenna Ortiz: ok pre-provision. for the dry-run can we simulate a traffic surge?
[05:06] Carlos Rivera: yes we can run a synthetic surge in staging and exercise the circuit breaker thresholds.
[05:12] Maya Chen: action item — Carlos will draft the cutover runbook with explicit gating checks, tie to metrics, and include rollback steps.
[05:23] Carlos Rivera: noted. I'll include canary duration, metric thresholds, A/B percent steps (1%, 5%, 15%, 50%) and explicit hold times.
[05:34] Samir Patel: can we add a semantic check gate after 5% and 15% before increasing?
[05:39] Carlos Rivera: yep that's the plan. manual hold at 5% and 15% for human check and automated semantic evaluation.
[05:48] Priya Nair: about logs and audit — we need per-request logs masked for PHI and retention at 1 year. is that supported?
[05:58] Maya Chen: yes we support configurable retention and field masking; we'll put the log schema in the runbook.
[06:06] Jenna Ortiz: will Redwood's console show token-level cost per route during the canary?
[06:12] Ellen Park: yes, console has per-route token cost breakdown; we'll also export a CSV for your finance team during the dry-run.
[06:22] Theo Marsh: on the network side, we need VPC peering and specific firewall ports. I'll send a list.
[06:28] Maya Chen: great, Theo. put it on the Jira or email and we'll coordinate.
[06:34] Samir Patel: one small thing — we saw a mismatch in sampling windows last week between our APM and Redwood traces, so spike alerts didn't line up. can we align trace windowing?
[06:45] Carlos Rivera: we can align TTL and tracing windows; we'll share the tracing config we use (span aggregation every 10s).
[06:52] Jenna Ortiz: for the A/B traffic duplication, do you write duplicates to the new model or just route a percent?
[06:58] Carlos Rivera: route a percent unless you want shadow testing; we can do shadow where you duplicate requests but don't surface responses - that costs more but is useful for offline eval.
[07:10] Liam O'Connor: prefer percent routing with optional shadowing for the first 24 hours.
[07:16] Maya Chen: noted. next, dry-run date proposal 2026-10-20, 16:00 UTC. available?
[07:24] Samir Patel: works for us.
[07:26] Jenna Ortiz: works.
[07:28] Priya Nair: I'll need the SSO test steps ahead of time.
[07:31] Maya Chen: we'll send the steps by 2026-10-15.
[07:35] Carlos Rivera: quick note on rollback automation: we recommend a circuit-breaker threshold of 1.5x baseline error rate or 20% semantic regression trigger to auto-fallback.
[07:48] Theo Marsh: auto-fallback is essential for us. please make sure it's documented.
[07:52] Carlos Rivera: will do.
[07:55] Ellen Park: also we'll provide a short video walkthrough of the runbook so on-call knows steps.
[08:02] Samir Patel: thanks. last question on data residency — some PII must stay in EU. we are US/EU split. how do we control region routing?
[08:13] Carlos Rivera: Redwood supports region routing policies. you can pin EU traffic to EU regions and keep inference in-region. we'll include the policy examples.
[08:24] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up, recap of next steps are in the action items. any final comments?
[08:31] Liam O'Connor: none from product.
[08:34] Priya Nair: no, thank you.
[08:36] Maya Chen: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with runbook, SOC2 boundary diagram, SSO steps, and schedule dry-run invite.
[08:45] Meeting ends.
